flawed_step: Step 2: the claim that every triangle-free graph has a vertex of degree at most 3 is false (e.g. the 4-regular triangle-free circulant C13(1,5), or K_{4,4}). No other argument can work, because triangle-free graphs of chromatic number 5 exist (Steps 5–8).
counterexample: The Mycielskian of the Grötzsch graph. Mycielski's construction M(G) takes G on v1..vn and adds new vertices u1..un and w, with ui joined to every neighbour of vi in G and w joined to every ui. Applying it to C5 gives the Grötzsch graph (11 vertices, triangle-free, chromatic number 4). Applying it again gives a 23-vertex triangle-free graph with chromatic number 5, so it is not 4-colourable.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof, with each step judged:
1. Induction on n = |V|. The graph with 1 vertex is 4-colourable. — Justified.
2. Every triangle-free graph has a vertex v with deg(v) ≤ 3. — NOT justified, and false. K_{4,4} is triangle-free and 4-regular, so every vertex has degree 4.
3. By induction G−v is 4-colourable. — Justified: G−v is triangle-free and smaller.
4. Give v a colour its at most 3 neighbours don't use. — Depends on Step 2, so it fails. Degeneracy only gives colourability with (degeneracy+1) colours, which is unbounded here.
The proof attempt fails at Step 2. The statement is in fact false:
5. Mycielski's construction M(G): add u1..un and w; ui is adjacent to N_G(vi), and w is adjacent to every ui. — This is a definition.
6. If G is triangle-free, so is M(G). — Justified. The u's are pairwise non-adjacent and w has no v-neighbours. So a triangle must be either ui,vj,vk with vj,vk in N(vi) adjacent, giving the triangle vi,vj,vk in G, or ui,w,vj, which is impossible since w is not adjacent to vj.
7. χ(M(G)) ≥ χ(G)+1. — Justified. Take a proper k-colouring c of M(G) and name colours so that c(w)=k. Then no ui has colour k. Recolour each vi with c(vi)=k to c(ui). This is still proper: if vj is not recoloured, c(vj)≠c(ui) because vj~ui; two recoloured vertices both had colour k, so they are not adjacent. The result is a proper colouring of G with k−1 colours.
8. χ(C5)=3, so the Grötzsch graph M(C5) has χ ≥ 4 and M(M(C5)) has χ ≥ 5. Both are triangle-free by Step 6. — Justified.
9. So a finite, simple, triangle-free graph with 23 vertices is not 4-colourable, and the statement is false. — Justified from Steps 6–8.
